From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Launch runway sync — exception matrix & rollout asks

Team —

We need a focused sync to lock the release runway and document exceptions before next week's exec review. Key asks: 

1) Product asks that are blocking the launch: feature-flag API (public schema + k/v rollout semantics) and billing events for metering. Who can own final sign-off?
2) Rollout plan: propose canary waves, enablement windows, and a rollback path if quality regressions hit.
3) Docs + CS enablement: owner for runbooks, quickstart, and internal troubleshooting checklist.

I've attached a working draft of an exception matrix and a timeline PDF. Please review and reply with: owner for each ask, any constraints, and a recommended canary cadence.

Proposed async deadline: EOD Friday, 26 Jun. If there are major blockers we should slot a 30-min triage tomorrow.

Attachments: [attachment: draft-exception-matrix.xlsx (xlsx)], [attachment: rollout-timeline-v2.pdf (pdf)]

Thanks,
David
David Kim
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Thanks David — quick notes from docs/enablement POV: 

- Docs owners: I can take ownership of the public quickstart + troubleshooting checklist. Will pair with Marissa on runtime-specific troubleshooting steps.
- Enablement: Recommend two live enablement sessions (pre-canary and pre-prod) and one recorded walkthrough for CS. Proposed dates in the attached timeline look OK but shift pre-prod by 48 hours to give ops breathing room.
- Exceptions: I reviewed the draft matrix. Two items to call out: (a) we need a documented fallback prompt template if we roll back to the safe model variant, and (b) approval flow for on-call ownership when an exception is triggered.

I'll update the Drive folder with a docs checklist by EOD Friday: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cLaunchDocs

—Laura

Adding infra/runtime constraints from my side: 

- Dedicated capacity: the reserved GPU pool we planned for this launch has a maintenance window on 6/29 (we were notified yesterday). We can do the canary but only two waves (canary 1: 1% traffic, canary 2: 10% traffic) before we have to pause. Full ramp to 100% will need a three-day window after the maintenance slot on 7/2.
- Fall back: recommend we keep the quantized safe-variant (redwood-small-q4) in registry as an automatic fallback for the first 48 hours post-rollout. Switching to fallback is a runtime config flip (INF-4821).
- Risk: billing-events hook is the riskiest in terms of ordering guarantees. If billing events aren't landed, we should gate the rollout behind a short-circuit that mutes metering and flags for manual reconciliation.

Reference: Jira INF-4821 — rollout gating/automatic-fallback (https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INF-4821).

I can take owner for the fallback plan and the runtime checklist. Need Marissa -> Laura sync to align on troubleshooting steps where GPU OOMs or perf regressions are suspected.

—Marissa
Principal Product Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Appreciate the updates. A few executive-level clarifications: 

- Approve exception path: I approve the two-stage canary and the automatic fallback approach for the initial 48-hour window. This keeps customer experience intact while we verify telemetry.
- Billing events: Legal needs to confirm whether muted metering during canary is acceptable contractually for customers. Aditya, please loop Legal (or product counsel) and confirm by EOD Friday. Sally (cc'ed) — if Acme plans to rely on billing events for their integration, flag now so we can coordinate a manual reconciliation route.
- Escalation RSVP: If quality regressions surface during canary, we will trigger the SLA exception flow outlined on page 3 of the draft-exception-matrix.xlsx. Laura, Marissa — make sure the on-call playbook lines up with that flow.

I'll brief execs on Monday; want a clean one-pager for them by COB tomorrow. David — can you own the one-pager?

—Vivek
VP, Product
Redwood Inference
